selection_rule: Select exactly the 'v1' instance of each of the 4 R2-11 semantic categories (coding, instruction, reasoning, summarization) from the already-frozen, outcome-independent R2-11 workload corpus. 'v1' is a POSITION-based rule (the first-indexed instance within each category in the frozen eval_manifest.json ordering), fixed before any reference to this selection's R2-11 retention outcome.

explicit_non_cherry_picking_disclosure.note: The R2-11 per-workload delta_bytes at 4 GiB for ALL 12 candidates is disclosed here specifically to demonstrate that 'v1' was not chosen because it showed the largest retention improvement. In 2 of 4 categories (reasoning, summarization), v1 happens to show the LARGEST improvement in its category; in the other 2 (coding, instruction), it does not -- instruction-v1 in particular shows an UNFAVORABLE (positive, i.e. predicted-protect worse) R2-11 delta, the single most unfavorable result among all 12 R2-11 workloads at the primary budget. A rule that excluded or avoided that case to produce a cleaner runtime story would be outcome-dependent selection; this rule does not do that -- it keeps the one workload most likely to show a null or unfavorable runtime result too.

rationale_for_subset_vs_full_12: Section 11 explicitly warns against reusing all 12 R2-11 workloads without justification, and section 24 flags the full 12x3x2x5=360-execution matrix as potentially too expensive. 4 workloads (one per category) preserves full category coverage while keeping the campaign a manageable 4x3x2x5=120 executions (plus discarded warmups), prioritizing measurement quality/control (more careful machine-state control, ABBA ordering, cooldowns) over brute-force corpus size, per section 24's explicit guidance to prefer quality over size.
generation_conditions_reused_from_r2_11: research2/workloads/r2_11/*.json prompts and n_predict=512 reused verbatim; no dedicated R2-12 corpus authored, since timing semantics (fixed prompt, fixed n_predict, greedy decoding) do not require different prompt content than R2-11 already provides.
